episode_title: How to Stop Guessing and Start Testing with Casey Hill, DoWhatWorks

real_qa.q: Why do customer logos consistently lose in A-B tests on B2B SaaS websites?
real_qa.r: Customer logos are static assets with no ability to engage, and if visitors do not recognize the first logos shown, it sends a negative signal. Additionally, logos provide no ability to validate whether companies currently work with a brand or worked with them years ago and churned. Casey Hill recommends attaching case studies to logos (like Clay and Hex do) or using toggles by business type (like Seven Shifts) to increase interactivity and relevance.
real_qa.requete: why customer logos lose A-B tests

real_qa.q: What percentage of split tests actually beat their control according to DoWhatWorks data?
real_qa.r: According to a study DoWhatWorks published, only 11% of split tests beat their controls, meaning people are running a ton of testing and spinning their gears because they are ineffective. The platform helps guide more educated testing across different areas to improve test efficiency.
real_qa.requete: DoWhatWorks percentage split tests beat controls

real_qa.q: Should B2B SaaS websites display one or two CTAs in the hero section?
real_qa.r: Two CTAs consistently win when tested head-to-head in the hero section because diverse traffic has different intent levels. Some visitors want to jump into a demo while others are not ready to talk to someone yet, so providing both a demo option and a self-serve module serves different customer segments better than forcing one high-value path.
real_qa.requete: one CTA versus two CTA hero section testing

real_qa.q: Is generic AI messaging effective in converting website visitors?
real_qa.r: Generic AI language like 'AI powered,' 'AI first,' and 'AI native' are essentially filler and do not drive conversions. Instead, outcome-focused language wins—for example, Zendesk says 'our agents provide 24/7 coverage for customer support' rather than mentioning AI. Hootsuite and GoDaddy both saw winning variants when they focused on the output of their AI rather than introducing the AI tool itself.
real_qa.requete: AI messaging conversion rates testing results

real_qa.q: What is the positioning logic for customer logos on a B2B SaaS website?
real_qa.r: The value proposition should be sold first—what you do, how you do it, why it is for me—before using trust signals like logos to bring visitors over the line. Placing logos at the very top before establishing value leads to diminishing returns because you are trying to build trust before convincing the visitor of relevance.
real_qa.requete: logo placement on website sales funnel

real_qa.q: Why do executives sometimes reject winning test variants in favor of AI messaging?
real_qa.r: Executives and investors often push for AI messaging for optics during funding rounds, even when data shows non-AI variants convert better. The venture market has shifted significant investment toward AI companies, so leaders want their brand associated with AI regardless of test results. Casey recommends involving stakeholders before running tests and securing approval to implement data-driven changes rather than fighting decisions after results are in.
real_qa.requete: why AI messaging used despite losing tests
